name: RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences
description: RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences is a specialist health sciences university on St Stephen's Green in Dublin, founded in 1784 as the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland. It teaches medicine, pharmacy, physiotherapy, nursing and other health programmes only, and its undergraduate degrees are awarded by the National University of Ireland.
whyIncluded: RCSI's five-year medicine track accepts Singapore-Cambridge A-Levels with AAA in three H2 subjects, including Chemistry plus Biology or Physics. Its medical degree is recognised by the Singapore Medical Council for practice in Singapore.

livingCosts.summary: RCSI says a student in Dublin spends about 12,000 to 17,000 euro a year; the midpoint over a 9-month year, with RCSI's own monthly figures for transport, books, clothes, phone and social life, and the rest split between rent and food.
livingCosts.notes: Rung B (official total with partial breakdown). RCSI 'Budgeting and banking' page: 'Recent figures for the cost of living for a student in Dublin have ranged between EUR 12,000 and 17,000 per year' depending on accommodation, excluding tuition; midpoint 14,500 / 9 months = 1,611.11 per month. The page itemises monthly: utilities 43, transport (Leap card) 120, books and materials 70, clothes 45, mobile 25, social life 130; it gives no rent or food figure. Transport = 120; personal = 70 + 45 + 25 + 130 = 270; the remainder 1,221.11 (which includes the 43 utilities) is split between housing and food in the Irish share ratio 0.56:0.18 -> housing 924.08, food 297.03. For reference RCSI's own Mercer Court single room is EUR 322/week (13,202 for 41 weeks in 2026/27), well above this average, so the range assumes cheaper shared or private rooms. The non-EU 'Fees and Funding FAQs' PDF repeats the 12,000-17,000 range. No academic year is stated; months = 9 (Irish academic year). Excluded: tuition, flights, one-off costs.

programmes.name: Medicine MB BCh BAO (school-leaver entry)
programmes.summary: Yearly tuition for international (non-EU) students entering in 2027/28, plus a one-off EUR 135 NUI registration fee. RCSI says fees rise about 2% a year.
programmes.notes: RCSI Undergraduate Medicine 'Fees and funding' page, School Leaver Non-EU fees for academic year 2027/28: 'Non-EU Medicine tuition fees EUR 62,000', 'NUI fee (once-off charge) EUR 135', total EUR 62,135. The page says 2026/27 fees will be published once available, so 2027/28 is the latest published year. Programme is 5 or 6 years (6 including the foundation year for school leavers; 6 used here). 'The Non-EU fees for Undergraduate Medicine are subject to annual increases. The inflationary increase has been in the order of 2% per annum for the past number of years.' RCSI's MB BCh BAO is on the Singapore Medical Council's list of registrable basic medical qualifications. No 2024/25 or 2025/26 non-EU figures were found. On 2026-10-13 RCSI's fees pages showed only the latest published Non-EU year and no fee-schedule PDF, and searches found no official earlier-year Non-EU figure, so earlier starts stay without a fee. 2026 row (2026-10-13, unofficial): College Council's RCSI guide (updated June 2026) states non-EU Undergraduate Medicine costs EUR 61,135 a year for 2026/27 (EUR 61,000 tuition + once-off EUR 135 NUI fee); The UKCAT People's RCSI guide also gives EUR 61,000 per year (2026/27). No dated third-party 2024/25 or 2025/26 non-EU figure was found (agent guides searched give only 2026/27). Round 5 (2026-10-13): the live RCSI page now shows Non-EU 2027/28 (EUR 62,000) and EU 2025/26 only; a search-engine snippet of an earlier version of the same page read 'Non-EU Medicine tuition fees EUR 60,000 ... Total fees (for academic year 2025/26) EUR 60,135', but that version is no longer online and no dated third-party page repeats it, so no 2025 row (lead for a future round). No 2024/25 figure found.

programmes.name: Pharmacy BSc (Hons) / MPharm
programmes.summary: Yearly list tuition for international students, plus EUR 515 of one-off charges. RCSI currently gives self-funded students a EUR 7,000 yearly scholarship off this fee.
programmes.notes: RCSI School of Pharmacy and Biomolecular Sciences 'Fees and funding' page, Non-EU fees for the 2026/27 academic year: 'Non-EU Pharmacy tuition fees EUR 25,000', 'RCSI Development Initiative Scholarship (EUR 7,000)', 'Health screening charge (once off charge) EUR 380', 'NUI fee (once off charge) EUR 135', 'Total fees (for academic year 2026/27) EUR 18,515'. RCSI's ATT fees page explains the Development Initiative scholarship is EUR 7,000 per annum to all privately funded students, reducing tuition to EUR 18,000 per annum, so EUR 18,000 is used as annual tuition and EUR 515 (380 + 135) as one-off fees. 5-year programme (BSc Hons after 4, MPharm after year 5). An additional International Pharmacy and Biomolecular Sciences Scholarship may reduce year 1 further; not applied. No 2024/25 or 2025/26 non-EU figures were found. Recorded at the EUR 25,000 list fee (not the EUR 18,000 net of RCSI's automatic EUR 7,000 scholarship) to match how other universities' fees are recorded before scholarships. On 2026-10-13 RCSI's fees pages showed only the latest published Non-EU year and no fee-schedule PDF, and searches found no official earlier-year Non-EU figure, so earlier starts stay without a fee. On 2026-10-13 agent guides (College Council, The UKCAT People) gave only 2026/27 figures (pharmacy 'in the region of EUR 25,000', undated basis) and no earlier-year non-EU fee, so earlier starts stay without a fee. Round 5 (2026-10-13): live pharmacy page shows Non-EU 2026/27 only (EU 2025/26 rows exist but not non-EU); rcsi.com sitemap has no fee-schedule PDFs. No 2024/2025 rows.

programmes.name: MSc Technologies and Analytics in Precision Medicine
programmes.summary: Tuition for international (non-EU) students for this 1-year full-time master's starting September 2027.
programmes.notes: RCSI 'Fees and funding' page for the MSc in Technologies and Analytics in Precision Medicine: in person, full-time, 1 year, start September 2027, Non-EU fees EUR 25,000. No other compulsory fees listed. No earlier-year non-EU figures were found. On 2026-10-13 RCSI's fees pages showed only the latest published Non-EU year and no fee-schedule PDF, and searches found no official earlier-year Non-EU figure, so earlier starts stay without a fee. On 2026-10-13 agent guides (College Council, The UKCAT People) gave only 2026/27 figures (pharmacy 'in the region of EUR 25,000', undated basis) and no earlier-year non-EU fee, so earlier starts stay without a fee. Round 5 (2026-10-13): the programme did have intakes in these years (course page quotes graduates 'Class of 2022/2023/2024/2025'), so the years are not no-intake. Old course URLs (/technologies-and-analytics-in-precision-medicine/...) now redirect to the current page (EUR 25,000 Non-EU, next start September 2027); the Aug 2023 brochure and the course FAQ PDF under /-/media/ return 404. No dated earlier non-EU fee found, so no 2024-2026 rows. Note the current page's payment schedule still refers to June 2026/January 2027 dates although the next start is given as September 2027.
